technique.how: Have the patient hold both arms outstretched with wrists dorsiflexed and fingers spread for 30 s (or squeeze your fingers, or protrude the tongue if the arms cannot be held up); watch for brief, irregular loss of posture with a flapping correction. Examine both sides; can also be elicited in the feet or with hip abduction in a supine patient.
technique.prerequisites: Patient awake enough to follow a command and sustain posture; a comatose patient cannot show asterixis.

interpretation.positive_finding: Bilateral asterixis indicates a metabolic or toxic encephalopathy: hepatic encephalopathy (grade 2 or higher, West Haven) in cirrhosis, hypercapnic respiratory failure, uraemia, or drug effect (valproate, carbamazepine, lithium, sedatives). It does not distinguish between these causes.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence does not exclude hepatic encephalopathy (covert/grade 1 HE and deep coma both lack asterixis) nor hypercapnia; interpret with the rest of the examination and an ammonia/blood gas as indicated.
interpretation.pitfalls: Asterixis is absent in stupor/coma and in minimal HE, so it is neither sensitive nor specific; unilateral asterixis suggests a contralateral structural brain lesion (stroke) rather than a metabolic cause.
interpretation.changes_what: Present: obtain blood gas (CO2), ammonia/liver tests, renal function and drug review; treat the identified cause. Absent: no change in workup for the presenting complaint.

sources.citation: Formentin C, Zarantonello L, Mangini C, Angeli P, Merkel C, Montagnese S. Clinical value of asterixis in 374 well-characterised patients with cirrhosis and varying degree of hepatic encephalopathy. Dig Liver Dis. 2020.
Vilstrup H, Amodio P, Bajaj J, Cordoba J, Ferenci P, Mullen KD, Weissenborn K, Wong P. Hepatic encephalopathy in chronic liver disease: 2014 Practice Guideline by AASLD and EASL. Hepatology. 2014.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on asterixis to grade encephalopathy in a stuporous or comatose patient (the sign disappears as HE deepens).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Asterixis with drowsiness in a COPD patient means probable acute hypercapnic failure: blood gas and NIV assessment now. In cirrhosis, new asterixis warrants a search for a precipitant (bleeding, infection, drugs).
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No interobserver data located in accessible sources.

extraction_notes: No accessible quantitative accuracy data. Formentin 2020 (PMID 31582327, Dig Liver Dis 52:235-236) is a 2-page letter; PubMed carries no abstract and it is not in PMC, so its sensitivity/specificity by HE grade could not be quoted. Crossref (doi 10.1016/j.dld.2019.09.003) returned title only. The open-access narrative review Rissardo 2024 (PMID 38541088, PMC text searched for 'Formentin', 'sensitiv', 'specific') cites Formentin but reproduces no numbers. Searches 'asterixis hepatic encephalopathy sensitivity specificity' (0 hits), 'asterixis[Title] hepatic encephalopathy' (case reports/reviews only). AASLD/EASL 2014 guideline cited for the West Haven grading (asterixis appears at grade 2); guideline abstract not available via e-utils, so the grading statement is from general knowledge (unverified recall).
